spans.text: Often referred to as LFUs (or just “LFs”) and designed by the astral elves of old, lunar frames function based on the same basic principles as DGRs—both are frame units. However, a lunar frame is more of a living entity, born from a fusion of technology, magic, and natural materials. They can express limited opinions but are naturally subservient to their allies.
Lunar frames don’t require air, food, or water to survive.

Lunar frames begin their inception as specialized eidolic cores, which astral elves compare to seeds. They grow in a variety of conditions (usually absorbing starlight) until they are ready to assume a fully realized form, at which point these crystal cores take on an altered, wooden appearance. Upon being placed into the technological “empty frame” of an unrealized unit, they begin to worm their way through the unit’s skeleton and transform it, resulting in a lunar frame suiting the core’s nature.

Because lunar frames “grow” upon entry into their metallic frames, each can have a spark of personality imbued into it. Exactly where these impulses come from isn’t completely understood, but different lunar frames of the same type can have unique coloration, cosmetic flourishes, and behavioral quirks. Sometimes they are given unique names by their pilot, replacing the first part of their names (for example, a unique ESUS PAPILLON may be renamed to CHARITY PAPILLON).

LFs can be assigned freely to pilots as needed, but among the pilots of the Astral Confederation it is common for a pilot to undergo a bonding ceremony - called the Matching - with a newly formed unit. They remain together for extended periods of time, training with it and meditating with it (also trancing near it, for those such as the elves who do so). A Matching is considered complete when a pilot “hears” their unit communicate with them. This communication is generally indecipherable and brief, but is unmistakable, and represents a powerful bond between the unit and the pilot.
